title: Beautiful Traditional Heart Vine Mehndi Design for Back Hand
descriptionParagraphs: A charming traditional mehndi design tailored for the back of the hand, featuring butterfly wing and lotus pattern. Rated as Medium, this pattern is perfect for a party.

Skin on the back of the hand is thinner than the palm, so the stain is usually lighter and fades sooner. Leaving the paste on for longer helps the colour develop. This pattern suits someone who is already comfortable with basic lines, dots and petals and wants to practise even spacing.

Application tips: Leave the paste on for at least four to six hours; the longer it stays, the deeper the stain. Dab a lemon and sugar mixture on the dried paste to keep it moist and stuck to the skin.

image.alt: Traditional Heart Vine mehndi design for back hand — beautiful henna pattern

faq.q: Is black henna safe?
faq.a: Natural henna is never black. Products sold as black henna often contain PPD, a hair-dye chemical that can cause skin reactions, so they are best avoided.

faq.q: How can I make my mehndi darker?
faq.a: Leave the paste on longer, seal it with lemon and sugar, keep the skin warm, and avoid water for the first day after removing the paste.

faq.q: Should I do a patch test before applying mehndi?
faq.a: Yes. Apply a small amount of the paste to the inner arm and wait 24 hours, especially if you have sensitive skin or are using a new cone.

title: Graceful Traditional Lotus Pattern Mehndi Design for Finger
descriptionParagraphs: A detailed traditional mehndi design designed for the fingers, featuring star cluster and ring pattern. Rated as Easy, this pattern is perfect for everyday.

Finger designs are quick to apply and dry fast, which makes them practical when time is short. Fingertips have thicker skin, so the stain there usually develops darker than on the rest of the hand. This is a beginner-friendly pattern: practise the main shapes on paper first, then copy them onto skin with a fine-tipped cone.

Application tips: Scrape the dried paste off instead of washing it, and keep the area away from water for the first 12 to 24 hours. The stain starts orange and darkens to reddish brown over 24 to 48 hours as it oxidises.

faq.q: How long does a mehndi stain last?
faq.a: A natural henna stain usually lasts one to three weeks. It fades faster on areas that are washed or rubbed often, such as the hands.

faq.q: What makes Arabic mehndi different from Indian mehndi?
faq.a: Arabic mehndi uses bold floral patterns with significant negative space, while Indian designs feature dense, full-coverage patterns with paisleys and fine detail.

faq.q: Is Arabic mehndi good for beginners?
faq.a: Yes, Arabic mehndi is considered the best starting style for beginners. The flowing, larger patterns are more forgiving than intricate Indian designs.

faq.q: How dark does Arabic mehndi stain?
faq.a: On palms and fingertips, Arabic mehndi stains a deep reddish-brown. On the back of the hand, expect a lighter orange-brown.
